claims.statement: Across the defined customer-cluster population (eu-1, us-1, ap-1), current query p95 latency is 140 ms versus a 100 ms baseline, and replication lag is 80 ms versus a 10 ms baseline.

The latency change decomposes to +40 ms from the 100 ms baseline (+40%); replication lag is 8× its 10 ms baseline. The source provides one common three-cluster population, so no mix or within-population rate decomposition is available beyond this total-versus-baseline comparison.
The rollout started 12 minutes before the recorded latency change and targeted the same three clusters; this is temporal association, not proof of causation.
The aligned latency and replication-lag deterioration warrants investigation of the targeted rollout and affected clusters; the evidence does not establish that the rollout caused the slowdown.

submission.summary: Investigate customer-facing slowdown: latency rose 40 ms (+40%) and replication lag rose from 10 ms to 80 ms (8×) across all 3 affected regions in the defined cluster population. Rollout timing is corroborative only.
